t_advice_summary_textbox.text: Certain gnomes lead to bright forests: orange, green, red and blue. The other gnomes will lead to dark forests. They will always appear in fixed pairs - one bright and one dark. I should pay attention to which gnomes lead to which forest and the outcome of arriving at that forest (e.g. the amount of mushrooms I can harvest there.). Size, hat type and position are irrelevant and I should focus on which gnome leads to which forest.

vb_textbox.text:
Gnomes will appear in pairs: there are 'bright' gnomes that will take you to the bright forest (these gnomes are orange, red, green and blue) and other gnomes that will take you to the dark forest (yellow, pink, purple and brown). The size of the gnomes, their positions, hat shapes etc. do not matter. You will be given a choice of a bright and dark gnome in each pair.
You want to try and reach the forest each time that contains the most mushrooms for harvest. I noticed that there would be 'streaks' of mushrooms in each of the forest. For example, if you are gaining 5-9 mushrooms (before the multiplier) in the bright forest, I would continue on there until the number of mushrooms falls to 4 or below for a couple of tries. At that point, I would switch to selecting the dark gnomes for a while.
There is a multiplier on some of the rounds - you will be shown 1x at the start, or 5x. This should not affect the number of mushrooms available for harvest, but it is good to play it safe on the 5x rounds as the number of mushrooms harvested will be multiplied by 5 when adding to your points total.
